claims.text: Tailored reactive force-field simulations can predict suitable processing conditions for RHEA/Cu composites.
The predicted processing conditions can enable a self-propagating reactive process during sintering.
Reactive sintering can form stabilizing interfacial phases that overcome the unfavorable positive heat of mixing in RHEA/Cu composites.
The initial RHEA/Cu powder mixture consists of separate phases.
The initial RHEA/Cu powder mixture has poor interfacial bonding.
Reactive spark-plasma-sintering conditions can be optimized using a reactive force field tailored to the RHEA–Cu system.
The proposed treatment uses high-temperature, high-pressure reactive sintering under a controlled atmosphere.
The sintering conditions replicate reactor operational contexts.
Nanoscale intermetallic or transitional phases form at the RHEA/Cu interface.
Optimized reactive-sintering parameters drive localized exothermic reactions.
The localized exothermic reactions overcome the positive mixing enthalpy of the RHEA/Cu system.
The reactions promote interfacial-phase formation that stabilizes the composite structure.
The process produces a large-scale, stable composite with continuous RHEA/Cu interfaces.
The resulting composite has greater mechanical strength than composites made by conventional techniques.
The resulting composite has greater irradiation resistance than composites made by conventional techniques.
Conventionally melted or cast RHEA/Cu composites suffer from elemental segregation.
Conventionally melted or cast RHEA/Cu composites have unstable interfacial bonding.
The proposed process is limited to RHEA/Cu systems treated under high-temperature sintering conditions.
The process may not work for other alloy combinations or lower-energy processes.
